content:
Following yesterday's wave of system updates containing security fixes, Apple has now detailed the security content of Safari 26.6.1. Here are the details.

Codex appears multiple times in the CVE acknowledgements list

Apple updated its "Apple security releases" webpage today, detailing the bug fixes in Safari 26.6.1, which is now available for download on macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia.

According to the document, this update contains 22 CVEs, all related to WebKit, including two vulnerabilities where "processing maliciously crafted web content [may] lead to memory corruption."

Interestingly, as with recent security updates, OpenAI Codex Security appears nine times, further highlighting the increasingly important role AI tools play in uncovering security vulnerabilities in Apple software.

Here is the complete security content from Apple for Safari 26.6.1:

Safari 26.6.1 was released on August 18, 2026. WebKit applies to: macOS Sonoma and macOS Sequoia. Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may cause Safari to crash unexpectedly. Description: An out-of-bounds access issue was addressed through improved bounds checking. WebKit Bugzilla: 317632. CVE-2026-64784: Janggoon Lee of Out of Bounds, OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit. Description: The issue was addressed through improved memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 313452. CVE-2026-43795: wwwlk. WebKit Bugzilla: 318348. CVE-2026-65338: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit. Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may lead to memory corruption. WebKit Bugzilla: 318405. CVE-2026-65341: Henock Habte. WebKit. Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed through improved locking. WebKit Bugzilla: 321480. CVE-2026-64782: Seonwook Kim, Shubham Chaskar, lattice, Josef Korbel. WebKit. Description: The issue was addressed through improved input validation. WebKit Bugzilla: 321484. CVE-2026-64781: Thomas Guillem. WebKit. Description: The issue was addressed through improved state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 321517. CVE-2026-65351: Niels Hofmans. WebKit Bugzilla: 316996. CVE-2026-65340: Claudio Bozzato and Francesco Benvenuto of Cisco Talos, Josef Korbel (Citadelo). WebKit Bugzilla: 317142. CVE-2026-65337: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit Bugzilla: 317349. CVE-2026-65336: Josef Korbel. WebKit Bugzilla: 316723. CVE-2026-65335: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit Bugzilla: 317603. CVE-2026-65333: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit Bugzilla: 317450. CVE-2026-65332: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit Bugzilla: 317611. CVE-2026-65331: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit. Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may cause a process to terminate unexpectedly. Description: A use-after-free issue was addressed through improved memory management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316347. CVE-2026-64715: Hossein Lotfi (@hosselot) of TrendAI Zero Day Initiative. WebKit. Description: The issue was addressed through improved checks. WebKit Bugzilla: 316918. CVE-2026-64780: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit. Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed through improved state management. WebKit Bugzilla: 316791. CVE-2026-65334: OpenAI Codex Security – Amy Burnett. WebKit. Description: A memory corruption issue was addressed through improved memory handling. WebKit Bugzilla: 317317. CVE-2026-43794: Dung Do (@_piers2) of Calif.io. WebKit. Impact: Processing maliciously crafted web content may cause a process to terminate unexpectedly. WebKit Bugzilla: 313703. CVE-2026-64787: Sugiyama Sota, Shubham Chaskar. WebKit History. Impact: Visiting a maliciously crafted website may lead to sensitive data disclosure. WebKit Bugzilla: 315528. CVE-2026-64778: Mohit Negi. WebKit Storage. WebKit Bugzilla: 321485. CVE-2026-64779: Shubham Chaskar, Tommy DeVoss from Braze Security Team (@thedawgyg). Additional acknowledgement. WebKit. We would like to thank Henock Habte for their assistance.
